transcript: I'm so glad I got to catch Color Theories in its final extension because I absolutely loved it. This is a piece by Julio Torres which he's performing at the rather nondescriptly named Performance Space New York. His says this isn't a play and I would agree. I think of it as part Ted talk, part comedy show, and part school lesson. It's largely a free flowing discussion of different colors and their characteristics, in abstract terms. He assigns concepts, places, energies, experiences, even systems to colors. Through all of this, he excavates some really astute observations about society and the spectrum of human behavior. A lot of this is through personal anecdotes, many of which are actually pretty mundane or universal. He adds uniquely humorous and creative perspectives to them that make you laugh, but then go “wait that's so true.” His delivery is conversational and almost meditative, which somehow makes it even funnier. And the production is whimsical and intimate, with the set being a massive book with various components that pop out for different purposes. All in all, a delightful experience and I hope that this is not the last time that New York audiences get to see it. With that, another program for my collection.
